comment: If you get stuck with this guy find religion bc only God can help you. The textbook he gave us wasnt even a real con law book and his lectures are useless, confusing, unhinged rants about nothing. Youre going to have to teach yourself everything but dont worry, the final exam isnt going to even be remotely related to the material you cover.

Professor Walsh may be the worst professor I have ever had. Nice guy, not mean or anything like that. He is just far too smart for the class he is teaching and refuses to teach to the level of his students. His lectures are impossible to follow, the class itself has no logical track, and asking questions usually just makes things more confusing.
His lectures go over your head and you will have to learn the material on your own.

He will talk about Scalia forever and ever. We used Gilbert as our textbook and had a midterm 30%of the grade. We also had a paper which was 3 pages long and 20% of the grade.   Avoid him if possible, worst professor ever...

He is so smart. So. So. So. Smart. It can be intimidating. He is also really nice. Once you realize the latter, it helps with the intimidation. Be brave. Ask for help. He is willing to give it. Study on your own. You're here to learn and learn to think for yourself. Not to have someone spoon feed you ideas to regurgitate onto a test for grades.

He's so smart that very few, if at all, will understand half the things he says on a good day. He's very passionate about his subject and clearly enjoys teaching it but unfortunately he fails to get his point across; while you are trying to take note on what he just said, he's already onto another topic leaving you hanging there like "what?"

Once you learn that on your BEST day you will never be as smart as Walsh, he become a LOT less intimidating. He tries his best to make all material approachable, and really cares about the students, but sometimes he goes over our heads. Otherwise a great guy!
